title: A simple and effective method to encapsulate tobacco mesophyll protoplasts to maintain cell viability☆
author: Lei, Qiao, et al.

steps.title: Isolate tobacco mesophyll protoplasts
steps.instruction: Prepare and isolate protoplasts from 40–60‑day‑old tobacco leaves, then assess their density and viability.

substeps.instruction: Take fully expanded tobacco leaves of similar growth state (40–60 days old).
Excise leaves, sterilize by rinsing with 75 % ethanol for 10 s, then with 0.1 % mercuric chloride for 4 min; wash 3–5 times with distilled water and dry on sterilized filter paper.
Remove large veins, pile 2–4 leaves, and cut the middle portion into 0.5–1.0 mm strips with a sharp razor blade, avoiding bruising.

Transfer leaf strips quickly into enzyme solution (4–6 leaves in 5–10 ml enzyme mix) using flat‑tip forceps; incubate in the dark at 25 ± 1 °C for 3.5 h with gentle spiralling until the solution turns green.
Wet a 100‑mesh stainless cell strainer (pore size 149 µm) with W5 solution, filter the enzyme suspension, and collect the filtrate in a 50 ml round‑bottom tube.
Centrifuge the filtrate at 79 × g for 4 min; discard supernatant without disturbing the protoplast pellet.

Resuspend the pellet in 5 ml WI by gentle swirling, centrifuge again at 79 × g for 4 min, discard supernatant, then resuspend in 3 ml WI. Gently add 5 ml of 23 % (w/v) sucrose to the bottom of the tube and centrifuge at 79 × g for 4 min.
Collect the inter‑phase containing protoplasts into a new 50 ml tube, add WI, centrifuge at 79 × g for 4 min, and discard supernatant.

Resuspend the final pellet in WI, count protoplasts with a haemocytometer (10× objective): load 15 µl into the chamber, count cells in the four 1 mm corner squares, calculate density as (average count per square) × 10⁴, and adjust to 2 × 10⁵ cells ml⁻¹ WI.
Stain an aliquot with fluorescein diacetate (FDA) to a final concentration of 0.01 % (w/v) and incubate 30 min.

Observe stained protoplasts on a confocal laser scanning microscope (10× objective) using 488 nm excitation; detect emission at 505–530 nm (green, viable) and 650–730 nm (red chloroplast autofluorescence). Count total and viable cells in ten fields, calculate viability as (viable/total) × 100 %, repeat three independent calculations and record the average.

steps.title: Immobilize protoplasts in Transwell
steps.instruction: Encapsulate the WI‑suspended protoplasts in a calcium‑alginate layer on a PET membrane, then overlay with a low‑sodium silica sol to form a silica/alginate composite.

substeps.instruction: Mix 50 µl protoplast suspension (in WI) with 50 µl 1 % (w/v) sodium alginate in a Petri dish; swirl gently.
Pipette 30 µl of the mixture onto the PET microporous membrane of a Transwell insert.
Add 200 µl of 0.025 M CaCl₂ solution to the lower compartment beneath the PET membrane; incubate 5 min at room temperature to form a calcium‑alginate thin film.
Remove the CaCl₂ solution and wash the lower compartment three times with 500 µl WI each, removing excess liquid with absorbent paper after each wash.

Prepare silica mixture: combine 200 µl low‑sodium silicic acid sol with 100 µl LUDOX® HS‑40 colloidal silica; adjust pH to 6.0–7.0 by adding 30 µl succinic acid solution and verify with pH test paper (Art. No. 92110, MACHEREY‑NAGEL, Germany).
Pipette 70 µl of the silica sol onto the calcium‑alginate film and let stand ~5 min until the silica sol gels into a soft silica gel.
Add 200 µl potassium citrate solution to the lower compartment and incubate at 4 °C for 30 min.
Remove potassium citrate solution and wash the Transwell insert 3–4 times with 500 µl WI each.
Add 500 µl WI to the lower compartment and store the immobilized protoplasts at 4 °C.

steps.title: Alternative ETAF immobilization method
steps.instruction: Embed protoplasts in a thin alginate layer on a glass slide using CaCl₂/mannitol/MES solution, then recover the layer.

substeps.instruction: Mix 50 µl protoplast suspension (in WI) with 50 µl 1 % (w/v) sodium alginate in a Petri dish; swirl gently.
Place 50 µl of 25 mM CaCl₂ solution containing 0.5 M mannitol and 4 mM MES (pH 5.8) on an autoclaved microscope slide; add the 100 µl protoplast/alginate mixture on top of the CaCl₂ drop.
Immediately cover the drop with a clean autoclaved coverglass; add 50 µl additional CaCl₂ solution at the edges of the coverglass to promote alginate cross‑linking; wait 5 min.
Carefully lift the coverglass with forceps, transferring the thin alginate layer containing embedded protoplasts into a sterilized Petri dish containing WI.

steps.title: Transfect immobilized protoplasts with plasmid DNA
steps.instruction: Introduce GFP‑expressing plasmid into the immobilized protoplasts using PEG‑mediated transfection.

substeps.instruction: Place the Transwell insert (with freshly immobilized protoplasts) into 500 µl MMG solution; incubate 20 min to replace WI with MMG, then transfer the insert to a clean, dry Transwell compartment.
Prepare DNA mix: combine 10 µl plasmid DNA solution (20 µg GFP plasmid) with 190 µl MMG solution; add this 200 µl mixture to the lower compartment.
Shake the Transwell at 80 rpm in an incubation shaker for 5 min at room temperature to allow DNA contact with protoplasts.
Add 110 µl PEG solution to the DNA mixture, mix thoroughly, and incubate at room temperature with gentle shaking (80 rpm) for 15 min.
Stop the transfection by adding 400 µl W5 solution at room temperature; mix gently.
Remove the transfection solution, wash the lower compartment with 500 µl WI and discard the wash.
Add 500 µl WI to the lower compartment and incubate at 25 °C for 20–24 h.
Observe GFP expression using a confocal laser scanning microscope with 100–400× magnification.

description: In this silica/alginate two-step immobilization procedure, we use Transwell as a support for immobilized protoplasts, which has three unique properties. (1) The tissue culture-treated membrane has a good affinity for the plant cell; thus, protoplasts can spread evenly and form a very thin layer. (2) There are more choices for membrane pore size, depending on corresponding applications. (3) It is very convenient to change or collect the solution without mechanically disturbing the protoplasts. We hope this simple and effective silica sol–gel/alginate two-step immobilization of protoplasts in Transwell will have great potential for applications in genetic transformation, metabolites production and migration assays.
